10.2f — Card Jam: Showcase

Card games hit different in an arcade row: you can watch a whole match over someone's shoulder, and the READ of a card game — the little math in the eyes — is visible. Jam season one ends today; the Create PT begins in three B days (11.1a). Play like it matters, because it does: your Create PT could be this game's descendant.

Showcase ~30 min

The arcade row, card edition. Same contract as 10.1f: host and player in equal measure. Watch specifically for the card-game-only moments:

  • The hesitation hover — the tester holds a card and reads it twice. Was it confusion or calculation? Your notes say which (confusion = design debt; calculation = design WINNING)
  • The rule question — anything you have to answer out loud is tomorrow's on-screen hint text
  • The rematch demand — the card game's highest compliment. Log which games got one

Star votes: best rule set, best card art (your 10.2b assets), best AI personality (10.2d — could you TELL what the AI wanted?).

Retro + Bridge ~15 min

Retro (same four quadrants, 10.1f format) plus ONE card-jam-only question:

  1. What did LISTS let your game do that single variables never could? (Name the exact moment in your game that is ONLY possible because of a list.)
  2. Was the starter's gift — the empty methods — a good learning design, or would building from zero have taught more? (This is an 9.10a fork-ethics question in disguise.)

The bridge to the Create PT — read this twice:

  • The Create PT (full guide) requires: a list, a procedure with a parameter, an algorithm with sequencing + selection + iteration, a call, input → output. Your card game HAS ALL SIX ALREADY — shuffle (list + iteration + selection), AI_Turn (algorithm + procedure), Deal (procedure + call), the score line (selection). Read the requirements against your own code and CHECK THEM OFF, out loud, today.
  • You may even PORT this jam's code as your PT starting point — the rules allow work you wrote in class. Fork yourself: 11.1a is three B days away, and it is not a new beginning; it is a continuation.

Tinker: Archive + tag

  1. git tag jam-card && git push --tags; RETRO.md update with star counts + rematch demand count.
  2. Write the 3-sentence PT candidate pitch: "As my Create PT I could ___ because it already has ___ and I would add ___." Bring it to 11.1a.

Reflect: your own code, read cold

Which requirement from the Create PT checklist was easiest to point at in your card jam code, and which one would you still have to explain carefully to a stranger — and why that difference?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Host + play in the showcase, collecting hover/rule/rematch data
  • Name the moment in your game only a list makes possible
  • Check off all six Create PT requirements against your own jam code
  • Arrive at the PT launch with a candidate pitch written
